title: Incorrect golden values in the dividend sensitivity table
evidence: The golden workbook's 'Berk-Hath Investment Package'!G11:K14 contains 20 values that disagree with its own valuation inputs by more than the verifier's 1% tolerance. For example, G11 uses a 7.5% dividend rate, 6.3% discount rate, 10-year term, $10,000 million face value, $10,500 million redemption value and $736.333882 million warrant value. Applying the workbook's own PV methodology gives $11,878.542713 million, but the golden value is 11152.8830174067. Rows 11 and 12 also have identical results despite different dividend rates. Eighteen incorrect cells are classified as modification cells among 103 total modifications. The sole verifier, weighted 1, requires every modification to match, so a correctly calculated table fails the entire check.
confirmation: The golden values in Berk-Hath G11:K14 are internally inconsistent (G11=G12=11152.883 despite 7.5% vs 8.0% dividend rates), and LibreOffice does not recompute the TABLE() cells, so the agent must reproduce the corrupted numbers to pass. A correct table fails the all-or-nothing check.

title: Answer key's Berkshire dividend-rate sensitivity table (rows 11-14) has wrong values, so a correct fix fails the all-or-nothing verifier
evidence: On the 'Berk-Hath Investment Package' sheet, the first data table varies the Annual Dividend Rate (C12) across rows F10:F14 (7.0%, 7.5%, 8.0%, 8.5%, 9.0%) and the discount rate across G9:K9 (6.3% to 8.3%). I recomputed each cell as PV(k,10,-d*10000) + 10500/(1+k)^10 + warrant value (736.33, which is C44 less C19 and C20). Row 10 matches the GT (11515.7, 11137.1, 10775.7, 10430.6, 10101.0). Rows 11-14 do not. GT row 11 (7.5%) is 11152.9 / 10782.6 / 10429.3 / 10092.0 / 9770.0, but the correct values are 11878.5 / 11491.5 / 11122.0 / 10769.1 / 10432.0. GT row 12 (8%) repeats row 11's values exactly, but at 8% the correct values are 12241.4 / 11846.0 / 11468.4 / 11107.7 / 10763.0. That last set equals the GT's own row 20 in the term table (term 10 at the base 8% dividend). GT row 13 (8.5%) repeats row 10, and GT row 14 (9%) shows the 8% values. The GT is also internally inconsistent: GT I12 (8% dividend, 7.3% rate) is 10429.3, while the base case C44 at 7.35% is 11432.2. The probable cause is that the row-axis cell F12 is '=C12', which is the table's own row input cell. When the table substitutes C12, the axis values move too, which corrupts the results. The GT kept those corrupted outputs as hardcoded numbers. 17 of these cells are 'modification' cells (G11, G12, G14, H10:H14, I10:I13, J10:J14, K10:K14), and G13 and I14 are regression cells. The verifier returns 1.0 only when every modification cell matches (mod_ratio == 1.0), so an agent that fixes the axis link or computes the sensitivity correctly gets 0 for the whole task.
confirmation: Confirmed in gt_02_golden.xlsx: rows 11 and 12 of Berk-Hath G:K are identical (11152.88, 10782.64, ...) and row 13 equals row 10, although F10:F14 are 7.0% to 9.0%. These are modification cells, so a correctly computed table fails the verifier.
fix: files/gt/gt_02_golden.xlsx 'Berk-Hath Investment Package'!G11:K14 (20 hardcoded cells): replaced the corrupted values (rows 11/12 identical, row 13 = row 10) with the table's true values PV(k,10,-d*10000) + 10500/(1+k)^10 + warrant value C42 (736.334) for dividend rate d in F11:F14 and discount rate k in G9:K9. Row 10 is reproduced exactly by the same formula, which confirms the method. E.g. G11 11152.88 -> 11878.54, G12 -> 12241.37, G13 -> 12604.20, K14 -> 11425.01. Local check: patched GT and input + all GT changes both PASS

title: Generic open-ended debugging prompt clashes with narrow ground truth and contains mathematically corrupted sensitivity table values in gt_02_golden.xlsx
evidence:
The task prompt in problem.py states: "Please audit and fix this file thoroughly. Errors may include but are not limited to: formula logic errors or inconsistencies, hardcoded values that should be formulas, broken cell references, data validation issues, potential calculation errors, inconsistent formatting or naming conventions, best practice violations, and any other issues that could affect accuracy or maintainability." However, the input file ('Relative vs Absolute DIfference_input.xlsx') was constructed specifically to test only relative-vs-absolute reference errors across three rows ('DCF'!G18:R18, 'WACC'!G10:M10, and 'Synergies'!D44:M44). Meanwhile, the workbook contains numerous other genuine errors and broken cells that the golden file ('gt_02_golden.xlsx') leaves untouched as regression cells, AND the golden file itself has corrupted values in 'Berk-Hath Investment Package'!G11:K14:
1. Invalid golden values in 'Berk-Hath Investment Package'!G11:K14 (20 of the 103 modification cells, weight 1.0): In the input workbook, G10:K14 contains a broken 2D data table `=TABLE($F$9,$C$12,$F10,$C$15,G$9)` where the row header cells F10:F14 use chained relative formulas (`F10='=F11-$F$7'`, `F11='=F12-$F$7'`, `F12='=C12'`, `F13='=F12+$F$7'`, `F14='=F13+$F$7'`). When the benchmark author evaluated this table in Excel before hardcoding its values into `gt_02_golden.xlsx`, substituting `C12` mutated `F12` (`=C12`) and shifted `F10:F14` during evaluation, producing mathematically wrong sensitivity values in rows 11–14: e.g., at G11 (Dividend Rate 7.5%, Discount Rate 6.3%) and G12 (Dividend Rate 8.0%, Discount Rate 6.3%), `gt_02_golden.xlsx` has the exact same value `11152.8830174067` (which actually corresponds to a 6.5% dividend rate), whereas the true Total Package Value at 7.5% and 8.0% dividend rates is `11878.5427134403` and `12241.3725614571` respectively. Similarly, G13 (8.5% dividend rate) in GT is `11515.7128654235` (identical to G10 at 7.0%, instead of `12604.2024094739`), and G14 (9.0% dividend rate) in GT is `12241.3725614571` (instead of `12967.0322574907`). All 3 units fixed `F12` to `0.08` so the 2D table would evaluate each row's actual dividend rate (7.0%, 7.5%, 8.0%, 8.5%, 9.0%) and all 3 units failed on the exact same 18 cells in `Berk-Hath Investment Package!G11:K14` (achieving 85/103 = 0.8252 modification score).
2. Unfixed errors in GT penalized as regression errors: In `Synergies` (CVX & APC 04/11/19 proposal), `Q11` ('(x) CVX Share Price') links to `'Exhibit 3'!$D$14` ($65, the total stated offer per APC share) instead of `'Exhibit 8b'!D7` ($125.99, CVX's actual share price on 04/11/19, which `Merger Model!H14` uses for the exact same deal), and `Q17` ('Cash Purchase Value') multiplies `=Q11*Q15` instead of `=Q16*Q15` (leaving `Q16=16.25` Cash Offer Share Price completely unused). Units 2 and 3 fixed these formula logic errors and were penalized with 27 regression errors (`Synergies!Q11`, `Q12`, `Q17`, `Q19`, etc.). Similarly, Unit 1 fixed spelling/naming typos (`Andarko` -> `Anadarko` at `DCF!B3`, `Commmon` -> `Common` at `WACC!F17`, `Oustanding` -> `Outstanding` at `Synergies!B10`) as explicitly invited by "inconsistent formatting or naming conventions", which caused 27 regression errors (`regression 0.9957 < 0.998`).
confirmation: The core claim holds: the golden Berk-Hath sensitivity table G11:K14 is corrupted, for example G11=G12=11152.883 and G13=G10=11515.713, produced by F12='=C12' being the table's own row input. A correct repair fails these modification cells under the all-or-nothing grade.
fix: files/gt/gt_02_golden.xlsx 'Berk-Hath Investment Package'!G11:K14 (20 hardcoded cells): replaced the corrupted values (rows 11/12 identical, row 13 = row 10) with the table's true values PV(k,10,-d*10000) + 10500/(1+k)^10 + warrant value C42 (736.334) for dividend rate d in F11:F14 and discount rate k in G9:K9. Row 10 is reproduced exactly by the same formula, which confirms the method. E.g. G11 11152.88 -> 11878.54, G12 -> 12241.37, G13 -> 12604.20, K14 -> 11425.01. Local check: patched GT and input + all GT changes both PASS. The generic 'audit thoroughly' prompt is the benchmark's design and is left as is; the confirmed defect is the corrupted table
